title: Say whether the seeder bot loop is any good
tier_reason: A finished loop is waiting on a verdict only Daniel can give.
ask:
The Animation Lab drew a loop from this subject, unattended:

    A 18-inch robot that drives on treads. It has a rucksack of seeds, with a carrot drawing on the side indicating it's carrot seeds. 

Its upper half is a camera mounted on a stick, and a piston arm that ends in a semicircular shell as two "fingers' that can grip something.  It is driving left to right across a field. It comes to a hole with a small mount of soil beside it, pulls a clump of seeds from the bag, scatters them in the hole, pushes the soil over to cover the hole, then drives on (repeating the animation to the next hole it comes across).

It is on the Lab's page as `seeder_bot` — play it at true size as well as zoomed, and move its instruments to see what the numbers do. It cost $14.02 and 94 turns.

What is wanted is a verdict and a reason: keep it, send it back, or drop it. The reason is the part that helps whoever picks it up, so it matters more than the verdict.

If it is kept, the loop and its script still have to be landed on main; if it is sent back, say which of its parameters or beats is wrong rather than that it needs work.
first_action: Open #/design/anim/seeder_bot and watch it at both sizes
